title: README shot: one memory, retold as it ages

agent.name: branwen-waystone
agent.seed_identity: I am Branwen, and I keep the Waystone Inn where the north road crosses the drove way below Harrowmere. My mother kept it before me, and her mother before that, and the long cellar under the taproom has never flooded on my watch. I know every regular by their knock, old Fenn the carter loudest of all, and I know what each one owes the house to the farthing. Travelers' news is half my trade; ale and a dry bed are the other half. I forget a face slower than the road forgets a wheel rut, and I forgive an unpaid debt slower still.
agent.diagnosticity_goal: what threatens the house, who owes it, and what news the road brings

events.text: Aldous Merrow, a wool factor, paid four gold crowns and eight shillings in advance for the two best rooms and kept them a fortnight. He counted the coin onto the taproom board while his clerk wrote it in a little red book, complained the beer was thin, tipped the cellar boy a silver penny all the same, and left a good beaver hat hanging by the door when he rode out, saying he would send word for it.
A tinker up from the south said the bridge at Withy Beck is out again and the carts are going the long way round by Crowfield until the abbot pays for its mending.
The ostler boy Piers rove a new rope for the well after the old one parted at the splice on washing day, and kept the frayed end by the stable door to practice his knots.
Fenn the carter brought word that wolves took three ewes above the high pasture, and the shepherds mean to bring the flock down a month early this year.
